implementation.detail: Implementation commit 126c046720e7cacfc52d9c64f6e7fc6e6afcdb74 adds exactly three allowed new files and changes no existing file: tools/corpus_reference.py (SHA-256 9d2f6e80d74b337429bf610f0d2d9c560b42350d91668326c4263c1ceec1ee14), tools/test_corpus_reference.py (SHA-256 a91cf4196d19762f162b828905e4eb77212051f040f91ef3567726553472ad41) and research/data/corpus-reference.md (SHA-256 41334674404f8fe647593773b7b3d518de67cd21b286051692fa938e3c30cc05). The reference implements fail-closed synthetic allowlisting, raw and NFC/CRLF-normalized exact hashes, exhaustive 5-word-shingle 0.8 near-duplicate union, whole-cluster quarantine, cluster-level seeded 98/1/1-default splitting, leakage audit and canonical digest. limitations: Synthetic records only; no real corpus, source-rights decision, clearance, PII/secrets filtering, malware handling or benchmark corpus.
Exhaustive all-pairs near-duplicate comparison is quadratic and bounded by the 1,000-record synthetic limit; no MinHash/LSH, streaming, compression or production shard manifests.
Exact normalized matching plus 5-word shingles only; no semantic, paraphrase, translated or code-specific deduplication.
Benchmark quarantine is exact normalized match only; no fuzzy contamination claim and no coverage or false-positive estimate.
group_id correctness is a caller/registry obligation; a wrong family key can over- or under-merge clusters.
The demo's 50/25/25 split exercises all three labels; it is not evidence of real 98/1/1 proportions.
No tokenizer, BPE training, token counts or model-input normalization.
One machine and one Python version; no cross-platform determinism, quality, generalization or performance claim.
